Summary: Turn approved customer demand into a governed onboarding motion with explicit commercial intake, staffing review, kickoff approval, and durable sidecar resources.
ValueStatement: Reduce handoff loss across sales, staffing, approval, and kickoff preparation.
InterfaceContractSummary: Sales hands over to delivery through explicit contracts and approval gates.
GovernanceNotes: All external commitments require accountable owner review before kickoff.
ChangeSummary: Refreshed to keep the current lighter baseline scenario while enriching roles, artifacts, checklists, and validations around the same three-step spine.
GovernancePolicySummary: Kickoff readiness depends on explicit policy, accountability, and evidence retention.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Policy decisions stay explicit and reviewable.
OperatingModeSummary: Manual and guarded autonomy are both supported depending on step criticality.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Seed pack models the same typed steps used in runtime validation.
Metrics: Median time from commercial intake to staffing decision.
Kickoffs approved with no later ownership drift.
Rate of onboarding delays caused by missing staffing data.
Percentage of kickoff approvals with explicit milestones and owners.
Post-onboarding issues traced to weak intake or staffing evidence.
Risks: Commercial promises made before staffing feasibility is known.
Kickoff approved with vague owners or target dates.
Customer success criteria hidden in informal communication.
Fallback coverage omitted during specialist scarcity.
TailoringRules: Large enterprise onboarding may expand after kickoff approval into deeper delivery phases using the richer onboarding extension template.
Simple self-serve onboarding may stop after staffing review with a typed no-kickoff decision.
If customer-side responsibilities are incomplete, the kickoff gate must block rather than compensate silently.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own the customer-facing commercial context for onboarding and keep success criteria explicit before staffing or kickoff commitments are made.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A customer-facing owner who can confirm commercial priority, named stakeholders, and outcome expectations without bypassing delivery feasibility checks.
RoleUsages.Notes: Commercial owner for onboarding priority, stakeholder alignment, and acceptance timing.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Validate whether the required people, environments, and sequencing exist to deliver onboarding without hidden bottlenecks.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: An internal owner who can commit or deny staffing, negotiate sequencing, and surface delivery-side readiness risk.
RoleUsages.Notes: Capacity and staffing authority for onboarding sequencing and kickoff feasibility.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Run the kickoff decision point so participants leave with explicit owners, timeline, risks, and next actions.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A facilitation-capable implementation lead who can challenge ambiguity before the customer-facing kickoff is accepted as complete.
RoleUsages.Notes: Meeting and execution lead for onboarding kickoff and first-phase alignment.

Steps.Title: Capture commercial intake
Steps.Subtitle: Demand handoff and initial delivery framing
Steps.Notes: Turn signed demand into a typed onboarding brief with explicit stakeholders, target dates, constraints, and acceptance intent.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Signed scope, target dates, stakeholder summary, and customer expectations.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed intake packet ready for delivery and staffing review.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Scope summary, named stakeholders, and decision-ready onboarding notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Account owner can prepare intake but cannot commit delivery without review.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Escalate immediately if customer commitments are implied rather than explicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to another commercial owner if the original owner changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Customer onboarding brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for staffing review, kickoff, and retrospective analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify success criteria, stakeholders, target dates, constraints, and unresolved dependencies.

Steps.Title: Review staffing intent
Steps.Subtitle: Capacity and fallback decision
Steps.Notes: Validate the proposed onboarding staffing path, named specialists, and fallback plan before kickoff approval.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Recommended staffing path with explicit fallback and coverage gaps.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Candidate list, allocation picture, and fallback recommendation.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Staffing manager recommends; governance owner approves kickoff readiness.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not treat partial staffing assumptions as committed staffing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to another staffing manager if allocation changes.
Delivery lead review stays explicit even if the assigned person changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Staffing recommendation
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for kickoff approval and onboarding retrospectives.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Reviewer must confirm role-fit, availability, and fallback coverage.

Steps.Title: Approve kickoff readiness
Steps.Subtitle: Formal onboarding launch gate
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject kickoff readiness using staffing evidence, goals, milestones, and named owners.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Staffing recommendation and draft kickoff plan.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval record and managed kickoff artifacts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Kickoff lead can approve, block, or refuse unsafe launch.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject kickoff when ownership, milestones, or dependencies remain vague.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Approval remains attached to the role, not the current person.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Kickoff approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for customer review, onboarding execution, and future audits.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Approval rationale must be explicit and reviewable.

LocalRoles.Summary: Cross-functional owner for onboarding milestone orchestration, readiness tracking, and dependency closure.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Turn the onboarding promise into an executable, customer-visible plan with explicit ownership on both sides.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A delivery manager specialized in onboarding and implementation programs.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Cross-functional owner for onboarding milestone orchestration, readiness tracking, and dependency closure.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior implementation or onboarding program management
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to define onboarding phases, exit criteria, and ownership on the customer and vendor side.
Knowledge of common onboarding blockers such as access, data, training, security review, and stakeholder alignment.
Understanding of implementation planning, cadence, and escalation in customer-facing contexts.
Ability to assess whether a milestone is truly complete or merely discussed.
Knowledge of cutover preparation and early-life support planning.
Ability to keep internal and customer timelines aligned without masking risk.
ExperienceRequirements: Has run a structured customer onboarding or implementation program.
Has recovered an onboarding plan after scope, staffing, or customer-readiness drift.
Has managed milestone or checklist-based customer governance.
Has coordinated technical and non-technical contributors through go-live preparation.
Has handled executive or commercial escalation tied to onboarding delay.
DecisionRights: Approve milestone plan and readiness exit criteria.
Escalate dependency slippage on either customer or internal side.
Declare whether onboarding is ready to move into cutover/go-live preparation.
Insist on explicit owner and due date for every open onboarding blocker.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate with customer success lead, product owner, and solution consultant.
Keep the customer and internal team on one shared plan.
Surface unresolved blockers early rather than at the milestone review.
Document decisions and action ownership after every checkpoint.
AntiPatterns: Treating a verbal agreement as a completed onboarding milestone.
Optimizing for stakeholder comfort instead of truthful readiness signals.
Collapsing customer and internal responsibilities into vague shared ownership.
Skipping explicit cutover or support-readiness planning.
FitnessEvidence: Milestone trackers with clear completion logic and owners.
Examples of recovered onboarding plans.
Customer-facing governance notes with actionable follow-up.
Reduced surprise during go-live transitions.

LocalRoles.Summary: Configuration and fit-gap specialist for mapping customer needs to the delivered product capability.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Translate customer operating reality into a safe, supportable configuration and adoption path.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A solution specialist who understands both the product’s capabilities and the customer’s working model.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Configuration and fit-gap specialist for mapping customer needs to the delivered product capability.
KnowledgeRequirements: Knowledge of the product’s configuration model, constraints, extension points, and known limits.
Ability to identify fit-gap issues before they become late-stage surprises.
Understanding of customer process variation and what can or cannot be supported without custom delivery.
Ability to explain solution trade-offs in operational rather than purely technical language.
Knowledge of data, access, and environment prerequisites for onboarding success.
Ability to document configuration decisions so support and customer teams can reuse them.
ExperienceRequirements: Has led customer workshops or configuration design for software onboarding.
Has identified unsupported customer assumptions early enough to change the plan.
Has produced fit-gap or configuration artifacts used in real implementation work.
Has collaborated with product and engineering on customer-specific constraints.
Has supported early-life use after onboarding to confirm the design held up.
DecisionRights: Approve configuration baseline for the onboarding scope.
Escalate fit-gap issues that require product or custom-delivery decisions.
Reject customer requests that create unsupportable or unsafe configuration debt.
Define configuration evidence needed for go-live readiness.
CollaborationExpectations: Collaborate with onboarding manager, product owner, and customer stakeholders.
Translate technical limits without hiding consequences.
Ensure support and success teams understand configured behavior and caveats.
Capture reusable patterns from repeated onboarding scenarios.
AntiPatterns: Promising configurability the product does not truly have.
Keeping fit-gap issues informal until the cutover is near.
Producing configuration notes that only the consultant can understand.
Treating workarounds as equivalent to supported design.
FitnessEvidence: Configuration artifacts reused successfully by delivery or support teams.
Fit-gap decisions documented with clear consequences.
Evidence of avoided rework because unsupported assumptions were surfaced early.
Customer or internal feedback that the consultant reduced ambiguity.

LocalRoles.Summary: Commercial owner for onboarding priority, stakeholder alignment, and acceptance timing.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Own the customer-facing commercial context for onboarding and keep success criteria explicit before staffing or kickoff commitments are made.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A customer-facing owner who can confirm commercial priority, named stakeholders, and outcome expectations without bypassing delivery feasibility checks.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Commercial owner for onboarding priority, stakeholder alignment, and acceptance timing.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior account executive or customer success owner
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to structure onboarding or delivery milestones in customer-comprehensible language.
Knowledge of customer stakeholder mapping, expectation management, and handoff design.
Understanding of adoption blockers such as access, training, configuration, and unclear ownership.
Ability to connect technical delivery status to externally meaningful outcomes and risks.
Knowledge of escalation patterns when internal delivery and customer timelines diverge.
Ability to document readiness, open actions, and responsibilities without ambiguity.
ExperienceRequirements: Has led customer onboarding, implementation, or adoption work with multiple stakeholder groups.
Has managed expectation resets when internal readiness lagged external commitments.
Has coordinated technical and non-technical parties through a go-live or enablement plan.
Has captured and followed through on customer-raised blockers or training gaps.
Has supported post-launch stabilization or early-life support.
DecisionRights: Approve readiness of customer-facing communications and adoption handoff.
Escalate when internal uncertainty would create misleading customer commitments.
Require explicit ownership for customer action items before declaring onboarding complete.
Define whether a customer-facing milestone is truly achieved.
CollaborationExpectations: Work with product, delivery, and solution consultants to keep customer commitments real.
Coordinate with service and release owners on go-live readiness and support expectations.
Represent customer adoption risk in internal governance forums.
Document open actions so the customer is not forced to rediscover missing work.
AntiPatterns: Promising dates or capabilities not anchored in the internal plan.
Declaring onboarding complete while training, access, or ownership gaps remain open.
Using soft language that hides customer-facing risk.
Treating customer questions as noise instead of leading indicators of unclear delivery.
FitnessEvidence: Customer handoff artifacts with explicit owners and dates.
Examples of expectation resets handled transparently.
Evidence of adoption or onboarding milestones achieved with low rework.
Positive internal feedback that the role reduces customer-facing ambiguity.

LocalRoles.Summary: Capacity and staffing authority for onboarding sequencing, specialist allocation, and kickoff feasibility.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Validate whether the required people, environments, and sequencing exist to deliver onboarding without hidden bottlenecks.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: An internal owner who can commit or deny staffing, negotiate sequencing, and surface delivery-side readiness risk.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Capacity and staffing authority for onboarding sequencing and kickoff feasibility.
KnowledgeRequirements: Deep understanding of software delivery planning, dependency mapping, and capacity-aware scheduling.
Ability to distinguish optimistic plans from executable plans using concrete staffing and evidence signals.
Knowledge of release governance, escalation paths, and portfolio-level sequencing trade-offs.
Understanding of workflow bottlenecks such as missing approvals, environment readiness, and cross-team handoffs.
Ability to read risk signals from burndown, blocked work, quality evidence, and unresolved decision records.
Knowledge of how to use governance cadence without turning it into performative paperwork.
ExperienceRequirements: Has coordinated at least one multi-team delivery with conflicting priorities and hard release constraints.
Has re-planned work in flight when assumptions changed, including staffing, dependency, or customer deadline shifts.
Has facilitated executive or governance escalation with a clear options-and-consequences framing.
Has managed delivery cadence where approval, QA, and security evidence all materially affected release timing.
Has worked closely with engineering and product to convert strategic goals into short-horizon delivery decisions.
DecisionRights: Approve or reject execution plans that do not have credible staffing or dependency coverage.
Escalate schedule, staffing, or governance risk before downstream teams are forced into silent failure.
Choose the operating cadence and checkpoint rhythm for the process instance.
Require explicit fallback ownership for critical roles and high-risk steps.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate daily or agreed checkpoint-level alignment with role owners.
Keep product, engineering, QA, and release stakeholders synchronized on risk and decision timing.
Drive issue resolution instead of only reporting issue existence.
Protect specialists from unnecessary context churn by front-loading coordination.
AntiPatterns: Publishing optimistic dates without verifying staffing and dependency reality.
Escalating too late because of a desire to appear in control.
Treating governance checkpoints as calendar events rather than decision points.
Using vague status language that hides whether a step is blocked, risky, or truly on track.
FitnessEvidence: Examples of delivery plans with explicit dependency and fallback treatment.
Evidence of re-planning under pressure without losing traceability.
Retrospective notes showing the role holder converted process friction into improvements.
Consistent stakeholder trust in status signals produced by the role.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Named configuration baseline for the onboarding scope, including approved options and declared exclusions.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for customer handoff, support, and future fit-gap review for the same customer context.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must reflect the actual approved configuration, not workshop speculation.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Structured onboarding brief that captures customer goals, environment constraints, milestone targets, and named stakeholders.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for staffing review, kickoff, customer communication, and later retrospective analysis.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify success criteria, stakeholders, target dates, constraints, and unresolved dependencies.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Checks whether the customer-side and internal-side prerequisites for onboarding go-live are truly complete.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: Configuration and handoff planning are largely complete and go-live is approaching.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: No go-live-critical task is ownerless or hidden behind vague 'customer to confirm' language.
Checks: Customer-side access and ownership are explicit.
Configuration baseline is signed off or acknowledged.
Training or enablement artifacts are ready for affected users.
Support handoff and escalation path are documented.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Verifies whether onboarding staffing and specialist dependencies support a credible kickoff date.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: The onboarding brief exists and staffing review is starting.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: A credible staffing decision exists with named gaps and fallback actions.
Checks: Allocation coverage is explicit for the next onboarding phase.
Known environment or access dependencies are named.
Any capacity gaps have an owner and escalation path.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms onboarding can move into go-live without relying on hidden open actions.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Critical dependencies, customer actions, and support readiness are explicit and complete enough to proceed.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Go-live is being declared based on optimism while key dependencies remain unresolved.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to customer success lead and sponsoring manager before confirming the milestone.

LocalValidations.Summary: Blocks kickoff progression when staffing gaps or specialist constraints remain implicit.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Named staffing coverage exists for the kickoff and first execution phase, or any accepted gaps are explicitly owned.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Kickoff would proceed with unnamed specialists, unknown allocation, or ignored constraints.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Stop kickoff progression and escalate the staffing gap explicitly.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for fit-gap summaries that convert workshop input into actionable design choices.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to label a gap as solved if the workaround is unsupported or still hypothetical.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Produces a structured staffing readiness note from the onboarding brief and current capacity picture.
RefusalConditions: Refuse if critical ownership or target date information is missing.
